clauses.label: sole paragraph
clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Civil Service Act 
(22 Stat. 403) and Section 1753 of the Revised Statutes, and as Presi­
dent of the United States, it is ordered that Executive Order No. 9721 
of May 10, 1946, as amended by Executive Order No. 10103 of 
February 1, 1950, providing for the transfer of personnel to public 
international organizations in which the United States Government 
participates be, and it is hereby, modified as follows:
The limitation in Section 1 relating to the period during which an 
employee shall be considered as on leave of absence from his employ­
ment with the Federal Government is waived with respect to Reginald 
C. Price, and he shall be considered to have been on leave of absence for 
the period March 9,1954, through September 12,1957, for the purpose 
of all rights and benefits provided by Executive Order No. 9721, as 
amended.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 11303 (1966-09-12, 31 FR 11963) modifies EO 9721, as amended by EO 10103, by waiving for Reginald C. Price the limitation in section 1 on the period during which an employee is considered on leave of absence, and deeming him on leave from March 9, 1954 through September 12, 1957 for the purpose of all rights and benefits under EO 9721. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11303.txt, 31 FR 11963, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed its number, title and date against the census register. The order is a single paragraph with one operative command, so the dossier's single clause is the complete inventory. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes EO 11303 by number (row "11303 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations") and also lists EO 9721. The first end is that express revocation. The waiver is a one-person act that took effect on the order's date; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 the exhausted waiver is distinguished from the surviving consequence (the credited leave period and the rights that rest on it), and no held source shows an earlier cessation of the command. The alternative reading, that the self-executing deeming was exhausted when the order took effect on 1966-09-12, is disclosed for the reviewer; I did not adopt it because the deeming operates 'for the purpose of all rights and benefits provided by' EO 9721, which stayed in force until EO 12553 revoked it. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: none; the order states no end date, only a past leave period (March 9, 1954 through September 12, 1957) that the waiver deems to have been leave. That period is the subject of the deeming, not a term of the command. No held later order other than EO 12553 names EO 11303; EO 12553 also lists the amended EO 9721, so the parent order ended the same day. The dossier's missing item for EO 10103 concerns an earlier amendment of the parent order, not an event after this order. Disclosed alternative end (not adopted): 1966-09-12, the order's own date, if the self-executing waiver is treated as exhausted when it took effect.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order contains only the waiver and deeming for one named person; it creates no appointment, fund or delegation. The surviving consequence is the person's credited leave status and the benefits resting on it, which the order recorded rather than continued as a command.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553; the credited leave status and accrued benefits are surviving consequences, separate from the exhausted waiver command.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full, with no 'in part' limitation in its table entry."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text), so the revocation does not preserve the order as a command. The credited leave period for the named employee and any rights and benefits that accrued under EO 9721 while it was in force are accrued consequences; the held sources do not show any open claim.

first_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11303 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
